newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: African Harvest to list in Johannesburg October 1.
newsitem.headline: African Harvest to list in Johannesburg October 1.

text.p: Financial services company African Harvest Ltd would list on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on October 1, Coronation Asset Management managing director Leon Campher said on Wednesday.
The company is a joint venture between Coronation Holdings Ltd, the National Empowerment Corp (NEC) -- a black empowerment consortium -- and trade unions.
Campher said African Harvest would be jointly owned by Coronation, the NEC and four trade unions.
"We have structured the deal so that at voting level we are 50/50 with the NEC and the others," he said.

"In terms of economic interests we have a large interest because we are putting up the bulk of the money, but we have an agreement that as African Harvest develops and deals are done...the consortium get a clawback of economic interest until they are 50/50."
Campher said the company's primary focus would initially be in three areas -- financial services, consumer services and deals linked to privatisation.
"African Harvest will not be an investment company, it will have operating divisions and the first one will be corporate finance," he said.
A Coronation Asset Management spokesman said more details would be released in the near future.
